resources.name: Signal PO
resources.description:
Purchase order confirmation triage system.

Auth: All routes (except the inbound webhook) use a session cookie. Sign in first — the client stores the cookie automatically for subsequent requests.

Inbound webhook: authenticated via `?token=<INBOUND_WEBHOOK_SECRET>` query param, no cookie needed.

resources.name: Auth
resources.description:
Session-based authentication. Sign in returns an HttpOnly `session_token` cookie. The client stores it automatically — all subsequent requests in this collection will be authenticated.

The cookie contains `<session-uuid>.<hmac-signature>`. Middleware validates the HMAC in Edge (no DB hit). Server routes additionally confirm the session row exists in the DB and has not expired. Sign out deletes the DB row, invalidating the session immediately.

resources.name: Sign in
resources.description:
Verifies credentials, writes a row to the `sessions` table, and sets an HttpOnly `session_token` cookie (SameSite=Lax, Secure in production).

Also sets `activeTeamId` in the session to the user's first team membership.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`
Errors: 401 on bad credentials.

resources.name: Get current session
resources.description:
Returns the current user and active team from the session cookie.

Returns: `{ user: { id, email, name }, activeTeamId }` or `{}` if not authenticated.

resources.name: Sign out
resources.description:
Deletes the session row from the DB and clears the `session_token` cookie. The session is invalid immediately — no grace period.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`

resources.name: Seed
resources.description: Dev-only helper. Creates 3 purchase orders and 5 supplier confirmation emails (matched, quantity short, delayed delivery, price deviation, unmatched PO) scoped to the active team.

resources.name: Seed mock data
resources.description:
Creates 3 POs and 5 emails covering all confirmation statuses. Jobs are enqueued but not processed — call POST /api/process-email afterward to run extraction.

Returns: `{ message, purchaseOrders: 3, emails: 5 }`

resources.name: Purchase Orders
resources.description: POs are the source of truth for what was ordered. Confirmations from suppliers are matched against these.

resources.name: List purchase orders
resources.description:
Returns all active POs for the session's active team, ordered by creation date.

Returns: `PurchaseOrder[]`

resources.name: Create purchase order
resources.description:
Creates a new PO scoped to the active team. `poNumber` must be unique per team.

`currency` defaults to `USD` if omitted.

Returns: `PurchaseOrder` (201)

resources.name: Emails
resources.description:
Emails are supplier confirmations. Two ingestion paths exist:

1. **Manual** — POST /api/emails (session auth, JSON or multipart)
2. **Webhook** — POST /api/emails/inbound (token auth, SendGrid or Postmark format)

Both paths store the email, save any attachments to disk, and enqueue a processing job. The job is not run automatically — call POST /api/process-email or POST /api/worker to execute it.

resources.name: List emails
resources.description:
Returns all emails for the active team, newest first.

Returns: `Email[]` — includes `status`, `hasAttachments`, `fromEmail`, `messageId`.

resources.name: Get email by ID
resources.description: Returns a single email row. 404 if not found or not owned by the active team.

resources.name: Ingest email — JSON body
resources.description:
Ingests an email without attachments. Use when pasting raw email text directly.

Required: `subject`, `emailBody`. Optional: `supplierName`, `messageId`, `fromEmail`.

Returns: `{ email, jobId, attachmentCount: 0 }` (201)

body.text:
{
  "subject": "RE: PO-2024-001 Confirmation",
  "supplierName": "Acme Components Ltd",
  "emailBody": "Dear Team,

We are pleased to confirm your purchase order PO-2024-001.

Order details:
- Quantity confirmed: 500 units
- Unit price: $12.50
- Estimated delivery: May 1, 2026

Thank you for your business.

Best regards,
Acme Components Ltd"
}

resources.name: Ingest email — multipart with attachment
resources.description:
Ingests an email with file attachments. Use `multipart/form-data` — do not set Content-Type manually; the client sets the boundary automatically.

Supported formats: PDF (text + OCR fallback), Excel (.xlsx, .xls), CSV, plain text, JPEG, PNG, WebP. Max 10 MB per file, up to 5 files.

Attachments are stored to disk (UPLOAD_DIR) and processed by the worker when the job runs.

Returns: `{ email, jobId, attachmentCount }` (201)

params.name: emailBody
params.value:
Dear Team,

Please find the confirmation attached.

Best regards,
Acme Components Ltd

params.name: attachments
params.description: Select a PDF, Excel (.xlsx/.xls), CSV, or image file (max 10 MB, up to 5 files)

resources.name: Ingest email — quantity short
resources.description: Scenario: supplier confirms fewer units than ordered. Produces a `needs_review` or `high_priority_flag` confirmation with a quantity mismatch.

body.text:
{
  "subject": "Order Confirmation - PO-2024-002",
  "supplierName": "Global Parts Inc",
  "emailBody": "Hello,

This is to confirm receipt and acceptance of your order PO-2024-002.

We can confirm 150 units (out of 200 requested) at $45.00 per unit.
The remaining 50 units will ship in a second batch.

Delivery date: May 10, 2026.

Regards,
Global Parts Inc"
}

resources.name: Ingest email — delivery delay
resources.description: Scenario: delivery date pushed past the expected date. Produces a date mismatch.

body.text:
{
  "subject": "PO-2024-003 - Delivery Delay Notice",
  "supplierName": "FastShip Supplies",
  "emailBody": "Dear Customer,

We regret to inform you that your order PO-2024-003 will be delayed.

Confirmed details:
- Quantity: 1000 units
- Unit price: $3.75
- NEW delivery date: May 20, 2026 (originally April 28)

We apologize for any inconvenience.

FastShip Supplies"
}

resources.name: Ingest email — price deviation
resources.description: Scenario: supplier raises unit price. Produces a price mismatch.

body.text:
{
  "subject": "Price Update - PO-2024-001 Amendment",
  "supplierName": "Acme Components Ltd",
  "emailBody": "Hi,

Please note a price amendment for PO-2024-001.

Due to increased raw material costs, the updated unit price is $14.00 (was $12.50).
Quantity remains 500 units, delivery May 1, 2026.

Please confirm acceptance.

Acme Components"
}

resources.name: Ingest email — unmatched PO
resources.description: Scenario: PO number extracted from the email does not match any PO in the database. Produces an `unmatched` confirmation.

body.text:
{
  "subject": "Confirmation for your recent order",
  "supplierName": "Unknown Supplier",
  "emailBody": "Hello,

Thanks for your order! We have processed order number PO-9999-XYZ.

Qty: 300 pieces
Price: $22.00 each
Ship date: sometime next month

Let us know if you have questions."
}

resources.name: Inbound webhook — Postmark
resources.description:
Postmark inbound webhook format. No session cookie required — authenticated via `?token=<INBOUND_WEBHOOK_SECRET>`.

Set your Postmark inbound stream URL to:
  https://yourdomain.com/api/emails/inbound?teamId=<team-uuid>&token=<secret>

Behaviour:
- Deduplicates by `MessageID` — returns `{ duplicate: true }` (200) if already seen.
- Strips quoted reply threads from `TextBody` before storing.
- Decodes base64 `Attachments[].Content`, validates MIME type, saves to UPLOAD_DIR.
- Enqueues a processing job automatically.

Returns: `{ emailId, jobId, attachmentCount }` (201) or `{ duplicate: true }` (200)

body.text:
{
  "From": "supplier@acme.com",
  "Subject": "RE: PO-2024-001 Confirmation",
  "MessageID": "<unique-message-id@mail.acme.com>",
  "TextBody": "Dear Team,

We confirm PO-2024-001.
Quantity: 500 units
Unit price: $12.50
Delivery: 2026-05-01

Best regards,
Acme",
  "HtmlBody": "",
  "Attachments": []
}

resources.name: Inbound webhook — SendGrid
resources.description:
SendGrid Inbound Parse format (multipart/form-data). No session cookie required.

Configure SendGrid Inbound Parse to POST to:
  https://yourdomain.com/api/emails/inbound?teamId=<team-uuid>&token=<secret>

SendGrid fields used:
- `from` — sender address stored as `fromEmail`
- `subject` — email subject
- `text` — plain text body (preferred over `html`)
- `headers` — raw headers string, parsed for `Message-ID`
- `attachment-info` — JSON map of attachment metadata keyed by slot name
- `attachment1` .. `attachment5` — file fields (up to 5, max 10 MB each)

Same deduplication, thread stripping, and job enqueue behaviour as the Postmark endpoint.

params.name: text
params.value:
Dear Team,

We confirm PO-2024-001.
Quantity: 500 units
Unit price: $12.50
Delivery: 2026-05-01

Best regards,
Acme

resources.name: Worker
resources.description: Processing runs on demand — there is no background daemon. Call one of these endpoints after ingesting emails to run extraction and PO matching.

resources.name: Process next job — Bearer auth
resources.description:
Picks the oldest `pending` job for `teamId`, claims it, and runs the full pipeline:
1. Downloads any pending attachments from disk and extracts text (PDF → text or OCR, Excel → tabular text, CSV, image → OCR).
2. Sends email body + attachment texts to the LLM for structured extraction.
3. Matches the extracted PO number against the team's purchase orders.
4. Compares confirmed qty / date / price against the PO and flags mismatches.
5. Saves a `parsed_confirmations` row and any `mismatches`.
6. Writes an audit log entry.

Requires `Authorization: Bearer <WORKER_SECRET>` and `teamId` in the JSON body.

Call repeatedly to drain the queue. Returns `{ processed: false }` when the queue is empty.

Returns: `{ processed, jobId, confirmationId }` or `{ processed, jobId, error }`

resources.name: Process next job — session auth
resources.description:
Same pipeline as POST /api/worker but uses the session cookie's `activeTeamId` instead of a Bearer token + body. Convenient for browser testing or calling from the UI.

Returns: `{ processed, jobId, confirmationId }` or `{ processed, jobId, error }`

resources.name: Teams
resources.description: Multi-tenant. Every resource (POs, emails, confirmations) is scoped to a team. A user can belong to multiple teams with a role of `owner`, `admin`, or `member`. The active team is stored in the session and can be switched without signing out.

resources.name: List my teams
resources.description:
Returns all teams the authenticated user belongs to, including their role in each.

Returns: `Array<{ id, name, slug, role, createdAt }>`

resources.name: Switch active team
resources.description:
Updates `activeTeamId` in the session cookie. User must be a member of the target team — returns 403 otherwise.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`

resources.name: Update team name
resources.description:
Renames the team. Only the team `owner` can do this — returns 403 for any other role.

Returns: updated `Team` object.

resources.name: Delete team
resources.description:
Deletes the team and cascades to all its POs, emails, confirmations, and member records. Only the team `owner` can do this.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`

resources.name: List team members
resources.description:
Returns all members of the team. The caller must be a member of the team.

Returns: `Array<{ id, userId, teamId, role, createdAt, user: { name, email } }>`

resources.name: Invite member
resources.description:
Adds an existing user (by email) to the team. `role` can be `owner`, `admin`, or `member` — defaults to `member`. Only the team `owner` can invite.

The user must already have a registered account. Returns 400 if the email is not found or the user is already a member.

Returns: `TeamMember` (201)

resources.name: Change member role
resources.description:
Changes a member's role. Valid values: `owner`, `admin`, `member`. Only the team `owner` can do this.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`

resources.name: Remove member
resources.description:
Removes a member from the team. Only the team `owner` can do this.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`

resources.name: Confirmations
resources.description: Parsed confirmations are created automatically by the worker after an email is processed. Each confirmation links an email to a PO (or flags it as unmatched) and records any mismatches in qty, date, or price.

resources.name: List confirmations
resources.description:
Returns all confirmations for the active team, newest first. Cached with a 30-second TTL; invalidated on any action.

Each item includes: `status` (`matched` | `needs_review` | `high_priority_flag` | `unmatched`), `confidence`, `mismatches[]`, and the linked email subject and PO number.

Returns: `ConfirmationWithDetails[]`

resources.name: Get confirmation by ID
resources.description: Returns a single confirmation with full mismatch details. 404 if not found or not owned by the active team.

resources.name: Approve confirmation
resources.description:
Marks the confirmation as approved. Sets `resolvedAt` and updates status to `matched`.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`

resources.name: Snooze confirmation
resources.description:
Snoozes the confirmation. Sets `snoozedUntil` to 48 hours from now — it will reappear in the action center after that.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`

resources.name: Resolve confirmation
resources.description:
Resolves the confirmation, acknowledging any mismatches and closing the item. Sets `resolvedAt`.

Returns: `{ ok: true }`
